0.long_answer: Methotrexate is a chemotherapy and immunosuppressive agent that was first developed in 1947. It is considered the first-line treatment for intraocular lymphoma, a variant of primary central nervous system lymphoma, due to its ability to effectively penetrate the blood-brain barrier. Methotrexate exerts its effects by inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase, an enzyme critical for DNA synthesis, thereby interfering with rapidly dividing cancer cells. Its development marked a significant milestone in oncologic therapy, and its efficacy in treating intraocular lymphoma underscores its continued role in clinical practice.
